requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

findings.claim: A null key on a positional record property is silently ignored instead of producing MsgPack005. A positional record property is declared by a ParameterSyntax, not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax, so GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null even though the property is declared in the current source. ReportIfLocatedInCompilation then discards the resulting diagnostic. For example, `[MessagePackObject] public partial record R([property: Key(null)] string Value);` receives no BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Add NullKeyOnPositionalRecordPropertyReportsMsgPack005, which runs the generator and all MessagePack analyzers on a source-declared partial record whose positional property has [property: Key(null)] and expects MsgPack005 on the Value identifier. On head, the diagnostic is absent because the helper cannot obtain a location from ParameterSyntax.

findings.claim: The `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` crash path fixed at TypeCollector.cs:985 has no regression test. None of the three added metadata-type cases has a member with `[Key(null)]`, so restoring the unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` indexing on this path would leave all added tests passing.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:985 delete-statement: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item) -> ((PropertyDeclarationSyntax)item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax()).Identifier.GetLocation(); expected to survive because the added tests cover valid keyed members and an unkeyed member (MemberNeedsKey), but never the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull branch. A closing regression test should define a metadata generic struct member with [Key(null)] and use its closed form from the usage compilation.

findings.claim: no test in the suite detects linq-first at src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1434

receipt_plan.detail: private static Location? GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(IPropertySymbol property) => (property.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax() as PropertyDeclarationSyntax)?.Identifier.GetLocation(); -> private static Location? GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(IPropertySymbol property) => (property.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.First()?.GetSyntax() as PropertyDeclarationSyntax)?.Identifier.GetLocation();

receipt_plan.detail: TypeCollector.cs:239 negate-condition: this.reportDiagnostic = reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null ? null : d => ReportIfLocatedInCompilation(reportAnalyzerDiagnostic, d); -> this.reportDiagnostic = reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is not null ? null : d => ReportIfLocatedInCompilation(reportAnalyzerDiagnostic, d);; TypeCollector.cs:239 delete-statement: this.reportDiagnostic = reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null ? null : d => ReportIfLocatedInCompilation(reportAnalyzerDiagnostic, d); -> (statement deleted); TypeCollector.cs:1448 delete-statement: sink(diagnostic); -> (statement deleted)

hunches.claim: Only two of the three unguarded DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] diagnostic paths identified in the requirement are changed. The remaining path at the reporter's TypeCollector.cs:735 can still evaluate the indexer before reportDiagnostic is invoked; the new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper runs too late to prevent that exception. Thus a metadata symbol that reaches this third diagnostic can still crash the analyzer or generator, contrary to the criterion that diagnostics requiring a source location must not crash for symbols without declaring syntax.

receipt_plan.detail: Inspect the remaining DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] access at the reporter-identified third diagnostic path (TypeCollector.cs:735 in the issue revision). The hunk changes only the accesses around new lines 982 and 1074. Diagnostic.Create arguments are evaluated before reportDiagnostic.Invoke and therefore before ReportIfLocatedInCompilation can filter the diagnostic, so FirstOrDefault-based location handling (or an equivalent source-symbol guard) is still required at the third access.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L8] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: Suppressing diagnostics for types and members defined in referenced assemblies is consistent with the product's deliberate ownership model: the defining assembly validates and formats its own types, so the consuming compilation need not report those member diagnostics.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed and receive no formatter or MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostics from the compiling assembly; the defining assembly owns validation and formatting.
